newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Commerce's Ehrlich says China a priority - RFTV.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Commerce's Ehrlich says China a priority - RFTV.

text.p: Commerce Undersecretary Everett Ehrlich said Thursday China remains a priority in the nation's efforts to promote the export of U.S. goods.

"We need to convince the Chinese that an open economy is part of the process of economic maturation," Ehrlich said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television. "They're the only major market in the world where American exports aren't growing along with the economy."
The outgoing Commerce Department official termed Japan's move to liberalize its markets "an incremental process."
On the domestic front, he said "there is some chance that" the federal budget could be balanced before the 2002 target.

"I don't think we should count on that," Ehrlich said. "It's certainly a possibility. The economy's ability to grow shouldn't be underestimated." But, he added: "We need to have conservative planning assumptions for that purpose."
The economy has outpaced the planning assumptions the Clinton administration has put into the budget in three out of four years, he said.
"That kind of conservative track record is what gives us credibility as we go into these negotiations and we go back to markets and offer them a budget policy," he added.
